song-aint-no-sunshine.title: Ain’t No Sunshine
facts: Bill Withers was working in a factory making toilet seats for 747 airplanes when he wrote this.
On the record he sings “I know” 26 times in a row. He meant to write more words there, but the band told him to leave it.
It won a Grammy for Best R&B Song.
listen: Listen for “I know, I know, I know…” How many can you count?
Listen for the questions he asks: where has she gone?
ask: We all have those gray days. What’s one thing that always cheers you up?
Is there someone you miss when they’re away?
Do you like sunny days or cloudy days best?
song-aint-no-sunshine.lyrics:
Ain't no sunshine when she's gone
It's not warm when she's away
Ain't no sunshine when she's gone
And she's always gone too long,
Anytime she goes away

Wonder this time where she's gone
Wonder if she's gone to stay
Ain't no sunshine when she's gone
And this house just ain't no home,
Anytime she goes away

And I know, I know, I know, I know
Hey, I ought to leave young thing alone
But ain't no sunshine when she's gone

song-all-i-have-to-do-is-dream.title: All I Have To Do Is Dream
facts: The Everly Brothers recorded this classic in just two takes.
It went to number one on the pop, country and R&B charts all at the same time.
It was written by a husband-and-wife team, Felice and Boudleaux Bryant.
listen: Listen for the word “dream.” It comes four times in a row!
Listen for the two brothers singing together in harmony.
ask: Who was your first ‘dream’ or celebrity crush when you were young?
Did you ever go to a dance with someone special?
Do you remember your dreams when you wake up?
song-all-i-have-to-do-is-dream.lyrics:
Dream, dream, dream, dream
When I want you in my arms,
When I want you and all your charms
Whenever I want you, all I have to do is
Dream, dream, dream, dream

When I feel blue in the night,
And I need you to hold me tight
Whenever I want you, all I have to do is
Dream

I can make you mine, taste your lips of wine,
Anytime, night or day
Only trouble is, gee whiz,
I’m dreamin' my life away

I need you so that I could die,
I love you so and that is why
Whenever I want you, all I have to do is
Dream, dream, dream, dream

song-the-bare-necessities.title: The Bare Necessities
facts: The songwriter originally wrote much darker songs for the film. Walt Disney replaced them all except this one.
Baloo the bear was voiced by bandleader Phil Harris.
It was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Song.
listen: Listen for the animals and bugs: bees and ants!
Listen for what the bees are making.
ask: What are the ‘bare necessities’ that make you happy every day?
Did you ever go to the movies to see a Disney film?
If you could be any animal for a day, which would you be?
song-the-bare-necessities.lyrics:
Look for the bare necessities,
The simple bare necessities
Forget about your worries and your strife

I mean the bare necessities,
Old Mother Nature's recipes
That brings the bare necessities of life

Wherever I wander, wherever I roam,
I couldn't be fonder of my big home
The bees are buzzin' in the tree
To make some honey just for me
When you look under the rocks and plants

And take a glance at the fancy ants,
Then maybe try a few…
The bare necessities of life will come to you,
They’ll come to you!

Look for the bare necessities,
The simple bare necessities
Forget about your worries and your strife

I mean the bare necessities,
That’s why a bear can rest at ease
With just the bare necessities of life

song-blackbird.title: Blackbird
facts: Paul McCartney wrote this as a symbol of hope during the Civil Rights movement in the 1960s.
Paul plays it alone on an acoustic guitar. You can hear a real blackbird singing on the record.
The guitar part was inspired by a piece by Bach.
listen: Listen for what the blackbird is learning to do.
Listen for the night and the light.
ask: Do you enjoy the sound of birds in the morning, or do they wake you up too early?
Did you ever feed the birds?
What helps you feel free?
song-blackbird.lyrics:
Blackbird singing in the dead of night,
Take these broken wings and learn to fly,
All your life
You were only waiting for this moment to arise

Blackbird singing in the dead of night
Take these sunken eyes and learn to see,
All your life,
You were only waiting for this moment to be free

Blackbird, fly,
Into the light of the dark black night

Blackbird singing in the dead of night
Take these broken wings and learn to fly,
All your life
You were only waiting for this moment to arise

song-blue-moon.title: Blue Moon
facts: It took three different sets of lyrics before this song finally became a hit.
The Marcels made a bouncy “bomp-ba-bomp” version that went to number one in 1961.
Elvis, Frank Sinatra and Billie Holiday all recorded it.
listen: Listen for the moon changing color at the end.
Listen for who the singer is praying for.
ask: Do you remember a ‘Blue Moon’ of your own? Or do you just like a good slow dance?
Did you ever go out walking under the moon?
Who was the best dancer you ever knew?
song-blue-moon.lyrics:
Blue moon,
You saw me standing alone
Without a dream in my heart,
Without a love of my own

Blue moon,
You knew just what I was there for
You heard me saying a prayer for,
Someone I really could care for

And then there suddenly appeared before me
The only one my arms will hold
I heard somebody whisper please adore me
And when I looked to the moon it turned to gold

Blue moon,
Now I'm no longer alone
Without a dream in my heart,
Without a love of my own

song-cant-help-falling-in-love.title: Can’t Help Falling In Love
facts: The melody is based on a French love song from 1784 called Plaisir d’amour.
Elvis sang it in the movie Blue Hawaii.
Elvis closed almost every concert in the 1970s with this song.
listen: Listen for the river flowing to the sea.
Listen for what the wise men say.
ask: Is there a song that always reminds you of your wedding day?
Did you ever see Elvis in a movie?
How did you meet someone you loved?
song-cant-help-falling-in-love.lyrics:
Wise men say only fools rush in

Shall I stay?
Would it be a sin
If I can't help falling in love with you?

Like a river flows,
Surely to the sea
Darling, so it goes,
Some things are meant to be

Take my hand,
Take my whole life, too
For I can't help falling in love with you

song-take-me-home-country-roads.title: Take Me Home, Country Roads
facts: John Denver had never actually been to West Virginia when this song was written!
He wrote it with a married couple, Bill Danoff and Taffy Nivert, who hadn’t been there either.
Today it is one of West Virginia’s official state songs.
listen: Listen for the mountains and the river.
Listen for the radio. What does it remind him of?
ask: Where is the place that truly feels like ‘home’ to you?
Did you grow up in the country or in the city?
Have you ever been to the mountains?
song-take-me-home-country-roads.lyrics:
Almost Heaven, West Virginia
Blue Ridge Mountains, Shenandoah River
Life is old there, older than the trees
Younger than the mountains, growin' like a breeze

[Chorus]
Country roads, take me home,
To the place I belong
West Virginia, mountain mama,
Take me home, country roads

All my memories gather 'round her
Miner's lady, stranger to blue water
Dark and dusty, painted on the sky
Misty taste of moonshine, teardrop in my eye

[Chorus]
Country roads, take me home,
To the place I belong
West Virginia, mountain mama,
Take me home, country roads

I hear her voice in the mornin' hour, she calls me
The radio reminds me of my home far away
Drivin' down the road, I get a feelin'
That I should've been home yesterday, yesterday

[Chorus]
Country roads, take me home,
To the place I belong
West Virginia, mountain mama,
Take me home, country roads

song-danny-boy.title: Danny Boy
facts: The words were written by an English lawyer, Frederic Weatherly, and set to the old Irish tune Londonderry Air.
His sister-in-law in America mailed him the tune, and it fit his poem perfectly.
It’s sung all over the world on St. Patrick’s Day.
listen: Listen for the pipes calling.
Listen for the seasons: summer, flowers and snow.
ask: Does this song remind you of family or perhaps a bit of Irish luck?
Did anyone in your family sing this song?
Have you ever heard bagpipes played?
song-danny-boy.lyrics:
Oh, Danny Boy, the pipes, the pipes are calling
From glen to glen, and down the mountainside,
The summer’s gone, and all the roses falling,
It’s you, it’s you must go, and I must bide.

But come ye back when summer’s in the meadow,
Or when the valley’s hushed and white with snow,
Tis I’ll be here in sunshine or in shadow,
Oh, Danny Boy, oh Danny Boy,
I love you so!

But when ye come, and all the flowers are dying,
If I am dead, as dead I well may be,
Ye’ll come and find the place where I am lying,
And kneel and say an Ave there for me;

And I shall hear, though soft you tread above me,
And all my grave will warmer, sweeter be,
For you will bend and tell me that you love me,
And I shall sleep in peace until you come to me!

song-the-end-of-the-world.title: The End of the World
facts: The words were written by Sylvia Dee, thinking of the grief of losing her father.
Skeeter Davis’s record went to number 2 on both the pop and country charts.
It was a hit again in many countries for years afterward.
listen: Listen for all the things that keep going: the sun, the sea, the birds and the stars.
Listen for the questions. Every verse starts with “Why…?”
ask: Have you ever had a song that perfectly matched how you were feeling?
Who do you like to talk to when you feel sad?
Do you like looking at the stars?
song-the-end-of-the-world.lyrics:
Why does the sun go on shining?
Why does the sea rush to shore?
Don't they know it's the end of the world?

Why do the birds go on singing?
Why do the stars glow above?
Don't they know it's the end of the world?
It ended when I lost your love

Why everything's the same as it was
I can't understand, no, I can't understand
How life goes on the way it does

Why does my heart go on beating?
Why do these eyes of mine cry?
Don't they know it's the end of the world?

song-fly-me-to-the-moon.title: Fly Me To The Moon
facts: This was the first music ever played on the Moon. Buzz Aldrin played it on a portable cassette player in 1969.
It was first called “In Other Words” when it was written in 1954.
Frank Sinatra recorded it with Count Basie’s band.

Fly me to the moon, Let me play among the stars
Let me see what spring is like on a-Jupiter and Mars

Fill my heart with song and let me sing for ever more
You are all I long for, All I worship and adore

song-folsom-prison-blues.title: Folsom Prison Blues
facts: Johnny Cash performed this live for the inmates at Folsom Prison in 1968.
Johnny Cash never served time in prison. He only spent a few nights in jail.
He wrote it after seeing a movie about Folsom Prison while he was in the Air Force.
listen: Listen for the train. Where is it headed?
Listen for the rich folks: what are they drinking and smoking?

I hear the train a-comin',
It's rolling 'round the bend
And I ain't seen the sunshine since I don't know when

And time keeps draggin' on
But that train keeps a-rollin' on down to San Antone

When I was just a baby my mama told me, "Son
Always be a good boy, don't ever play with guns"

When I hear that whistle blowing,
I hang my head and cry

song-ghost-riders-in-the-sky.title: Ghost Riders In The Sky
facts: The songwriter, Stan Jones, heard this legend from an old cowboy when he was 12 years old.
Stan Jones later worked as a park ranger in Death Valley.
Vaughn Monroe’s version was a number one hit in 1949.

song-home-on-the-range.title: Home On The Range
facts: This is the official state song of Kansas. It was written by a doctor in a cabin.
Dr. Brewster Higley wrote it as a poem, and his friend Daniel Kelley wrote the tune.
President Franklin Roosevelt called it his favorite song.
listen: Listen for the animals: buffalo, deer and antelope.
Listen for the sky. Is it cloudy?

Oh, give me a home where the buffalo roam,

And the skies are not cloudy all day.

[Chorus]
Home, home on the range,
Where the deer and the antelope play;

And the skies are not cloudy all day.

facts: It’s a traditional folk song from Veracruz, Mexico, long played at weddings.

A 1987 movie about his life brought it back, and the band Los Lobos took it to number one.
